data_fields.name: idle_weight
data_fields.donor_constant: uint8 per entry; roll is integer 0-99; entry wins when roll < weight; remainder means no idle

data_fields.name: clip_speed
data_fields.donor_constant: must be > 0 (ignored otherwise); idle forced to 1.0

data_fields.name: timed_play_length
data_fields.donor_constant: seconds; 0 = clip length / speed; negative = until replaced

data_fields.name: skip_cap
data_fields.donor_constant: none in donor; uint8 result, values above 255 are out of range

data_fields.name: transition_time_s (proposed, not in donor)
data_fields.donor_constant: read from MDL and stored; never read in this tree

best_idea: One clip per actor where a timed request interrupts at the next tick and a finished clip falls back to a weighted, rolled idle, with a distance-based update skip that carries the skipped time forward.
decision_why: The one-channel rules (timed request, one-loop idle that re-rolls, loop count, speed) fit hero and creature rigs, but the donor has no cross-fade, no hit timing and a global random idle roll, so Frankendom adds those itself and keeps hit frames in the engine.
acceptance: In the Pit the hero's attack clip plays at its authored speed and returns to idle with no visible hold, and a server test asserts the hit frame comes from the duel-step data, never from the clip length.
